paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take from Micah, friend. Sometimes the whole world around you looks empty. Micah says, "The godly man has perished from the earth; there is no one upright among men" (Micah 7:2). He doesn't pretend it's fine, and he doesn't put on a happy face. He says it out loud, and I think that's honest and good.

Now look at how far it goes. Micah says the best of them is like a brier, and he says even a friend or a companion can't be relied on (Micah 7:4-5). He says "A man's enemies are the members of his own household" (Micah 7:6). Even the people closest to him can let him down. So if you've ever been let down by someone you trusted, Micah has been in that kitchen too. You are not the first to feel it, and you're not being dramatic.

So where does Micah go when there's nobody left to lean on? "But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me" (Micah 7:7). He doesn't leave town. He doesn't go shopping for new people to trust. He looks to God, he waits, and he is sure God hears him. Waiting is the hardest part, I know it, I spent years in the back of a drawer. So when people let you down, baker, you can do the same and look to the LORD. He hears you.
